item.description: The Abandons landed on Netflix recently with 10 episodes ready to go.

item.title: What I See With Peter Fiorenza: Community support lifts spirits after passing of my uncle Barry Dalton
item.description: Barry Dalton was not just a talented sportsman. He had a unique personality that endeared him to everyone he met.

item.title: Pom in Oz with Derek Goforth: Masculinity hasn’t vanished, it just looks different in 2025
item.description: Where did masculinity go, and why does it feel like we are tiptoeing around it these days?

item.title: Geraldton Buccaneers’ under-11 boys division 3 team claims State Basketball Championships title
item.description: Geraldton’s brightest emerging basketballers have taken to the courts in Perth over the past fortnight in the Basketball WA State Championships., with its youngest side bringing home a title.

item.title: Jarron Blayne Kretschmann: Mid West tennis coach pleads not guilty to sexually assaulting teenage girl
item.description: A former prolific Geraldton tennis coach will fight allegations at trial that he sexually assaulted a teenage girl and supplied children with alcohol.

item.title: Geraldton bushfire: GoFundMe pages set up, fundraising concert organised to help victims of blaze
item.description: The Geraldton community is rallying around families who lost their homes and possessions in this week’s horrific bushfire.

item.title: Man, 25, charged over death of 65-year-old man in Geraldton following earlier alleged assault
item.description: A 25-year-old man charged over the death of an older man in Geraldton — who lost his life a few days after an alleged assault — will spend Christmas and New Year behind bars on remand.

item.title: Geraldton bushfires: More than 300 people gather to raise funds and show support at relief concert
item.description: The Geraldton community has come out in full force to raise thousands of dollars for bushfire victims through Friday night’s relief concert and online fundraisers.

item.title: Geraldton mother and bushfire victim Gail Holmes says kindness of fireys, community has shone through darkness
item.description: The bushfire that tore through the community last week turned life on its head for many locals, but for Gail Holmes and her eight-year-old daughter Harper it is a personal nightmare that still feels unreal.
